questions.q: Which statement best describes serum sodium threshold?
questions.exp: The chapter defines hyponatremia as Na below 135 mEq/L. (Book p962)

questions.q: Match the key concept in hypotonicity with its correct interpretation.
opts: Low serum osmolality with low sodium
questions.exp: True hypotonic hyponatremia has low sodium and low osmolality. (Book p962)

questions.q: A patient is being evaluated for urine osmolality below 100. Which finding or action is most appropriate?
questions.exp: Very dilute urine indicates appropriate ADH suppression. (Book p962)

questions.q: In the context of effective osmoles, the principal ___ is:
questions.exp: Effective osmoles draw water extracellularly and lower measured sodium. (Book p962)

questions.q: Which option is the odd one out regarding extrarenal sodium loss?
opts: Low urine sodium with gastrointestinal loss
Absent urine sodium in all renal losses
questions.exp: The kidney conserves sodium during extrarenal volume loss. (Book p963)

questions.q: Assess these statements about initial volume replacement: I the first statement is correct; II the second statement is incorrect.
questions.exp: Volume restoration treats hypovolemic hyponatremia. (Book p963)

questions.q: What is the characteristic value or relationship for SIADH volume status?
opts: Marked peripheral edema in every case
questions.exp: SIADH is classically euvolemic with inappropriately concentrated urine. (Book p963)

questions.q: A clinical decision depends on SIADH urine. Which choice is best?
questions.exp: ADH activity persists despite low plasma osmolality. (Book p963)

questions.q: Which statement best describes cirrhosis mechanism?
opts: Low effective arterial volume drives non-osmotic ADH
Total sodium depletion as the sole defect
questions.exp: Edema can coexist with low effective arterial circulation. (Book p963)

questions.q: Match the key concept in endocrine exclusion with its correct interpretation.
questions.exp: Adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism can mimic euvolemic hyponatremia. (Book p963)

questions.q: A patient is being evaluated for severe symptoms. Which finding or action is most appropriate?
questions.exp: Seizures or severe neurologic symptoms warrant cautious hypertonic saline. (Book p964)

questions.q: In the context of chronic overcorrection, the principal ___ is:
questions.exp: Rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia risks osmotic demyelination. (Book p964)

questions.q: Which option is the odd one out regarding correction strategy?
opts: Small controlled early rise rather than normalization
questions.exp: Correction targets must account for duration and symptoms. (Book p964)

questions.q: Assess these statements about desmopressin rescue: I the first statement is correct; II the second statement is incorrect.
questions.exp: Desmopressin can clamp an unexpectedly rapid correction. (Book p964)

questions.q: What is the characteristic value or relationship for fluid restriction?
opts: A way to increase free-water intake
First measure for many SIADH patients
questions.exp: Fluid restriction is central in euvolemic water-retaining states. (Book p964)

questions.q: A clinical decision depends on overcorrection prevention. Which choice is best?
opts: Use glucose as the only endpoint
questions.exp: Frequent measurements prevent unnoticed excessive correction. (Book p964)
